note: Reviewer-private verification harness. Production code is untouched on this branch; the branch merges the PR head (aac6056d) so the harness compiles natively, and the only additions are the pr416_*_test.go harness files and this docs/verification tree. Round 3 reviewed the dcc7104a..aac6056d delta, which REVERTED round 2's grandfathering: validateNoNewDeprecatedWorkloadTypes is deleted and ValidateUpdate is back to the strict whole-object check for both RoleBasedGroup and RoleBasedGroupSet. That is a deliberate scope decision (documented consistently in six places as 'fresh installation only'), so F2a/F2c/F9/F10/R2-F13 are red-by-design rather than regressions -- and their acceptability rests entirely on the fresh-install premise, which R3-F22 shows is enforced nowhere. 11 round-2 tests that encoded the grandfathering contract were retired via r3RetireGrandfatheringAssertion rather than reported as failures.

findings.title: The shipped default is the OPPOSITE of the documented default, so the PR does not remove any RBAC by default and its stated purpose is unmet
findings.detail: deploy/helm/rbgs/values.yaml sets `compatibility.v1alpha1.enabled: true`. Three independent places say the default is `false`: the chart README's value table (`| `false` |`), the chart README prose ("By default (compatibility.v1alpha1.enabled=false), the chart ships in restricted mode for security"), and the PR description itself ("(default: `false`)" and "When disabled (default): ClusterRole omits RBAC for deployments/statefulsets/leaderworkersets"). The PR's stated sole purpose is "to remove the excessive RBAC permissions introduced by v1alpha1 API compatibility before the upcoming release" -- with the shipped default that does not happen for anyone who does not opt in explicitly.
findings.observed: A default `helm template rbgs deploy/helm/rbgs` grants all 8 legacy RBAC entries (deployments, deployments/finalizers, deployments/status, statefulsets, statefulsets/finalizers, statefulsets/status, leaderworkersets, leaderworkersets/status) and emits NO --disable-v1alpha1-compatibility argument.
findings.control: The same render with --set compatibility.v1alpha1.enabled=false yields 0 legacy entries, proving the conditional itself works and the result is purely the default's doing.
findings.biteCheck: 90-bite-check.sh flips values.yaml to false, re-runs 01-helm-default-rbac.sh, and it PASSES; the edit is then reverted and the production diff verified empty.
findings.suggestion: Either set values.yaml to `enabled: false` to match the documentation and the PR's purpose, or change the README table, README prose and PR description to say the default is `true`. Given the PR is explicitly a pre-release RBAC reduction, the former is almost certainly intended. This is the third round in a row where the Go/chart default has disagreed with the documentation (see pr413-F1).
findings.round2Note: Shipped default, README table, README prose, NOTES.txt and the Go flag default all agree on true, and the toggle is effective: =false removes all 8 deprecated-workload RBAC lines while the =true control keeps them.

round3.note: shipped default matches documented default and the toggle is effective

findings.title: An RBG that already exists with a legacy workload type can never be reconciled again: the controller's own write is denied by this PR's webhook, forever, with no explanation
findings.detail: The new validating webhook rule covers UPDATE on `rolebasedgroups`. ensureDiscoveryConfigMode (rolebasedgroup_controller.go:339-370) patches an annotation onto the MAIN RBG resource on the first reconcile of any RBG that lacks the discovery-config-mode annotation -- i.e. every RBG created before this controller build. With compatibility disabled that patch is rejected by validateNoLegacyWorkloads, ensureDiscoveryConfigMode returns (requeue=true, err), Reconcile returns the error, and controller-runtime retries with exponential backoff indefinitely. PR#414 at least set a terminal LegacyWorkloadsDisabled condition via handleLegacyWorkloads; PR#416 removed that function entirely, so there is no condition and no event -- an operator sees only a silently error-looping controller. This state is not exotic: the PR's own prescribed update path is uninstall-and-reinstall, and the CRDs are NOT Helm-managed (no crds/ dir; they come from the crd-upgrade Job), so all pre-existing RBG objects survive and land in exactly this state.
findings.observed: For all three legacy types: patch attempts=1, requeue=true, err='rolebasedgroups.workloads.x-k8s.io "preexisting-legacy" is forbidden: spec.roles[0] (role "worker"): workload type "<type>" is not supported when v1alpha1 compatibility is disabled', and conditions=0 on the RBG afterwards.
findings.harnessBites: The injected denial is not invented: TestVerifyPR416_F2b derives it from the REAL RoleBasedGroupValidator (with a real Client, so its own nil-client guard does not fire) and asserts the same validator ACCEPTS the identical object when compatibility is enabled. The test also fails loudly if the controller never attempts the patch, so it cannot pass vacuously.
findings.suggestion: Restore a Step-0 guard equivalent to PR#414's handleLegacyWorkloads: detect legacy roles, set a terminal, explanatory condition (+ event) on the RBG, and stop without an error -- or exempt the controller's own housekeeping writes from the legacy-workload rejection. Degrading per role rather than per group would be better still.
findings.round2Note: validateNoNewDeprecatedWorkloadTypes exempts a role whose workload type is unchanged, so the discovery-mode annotation patch at rolebasedgroup_controller.go:363 is now accepted. Proved end-to-end against the real ensureDiscoveryConfigMode.

round3.note: grandfathering reverted at aac6056d; the controller's annotation patch is denied again. Unreachable only if R3-F22 is closed

findings.title: HARNESS-BITES CHECK for F2a: the injected admission denial is verbatim what the real validator produces, and the same object is accepted when compatibility is enabled
findings.detail: Kept in the harness permanently so F2a can never drift into asserting a fiction.
findings.round2Note: This was the harness-bites control for F2a and asserted that the real validator DENIES the update. The fix inverted that premise, so the test now reports HARNESS PROBLEM by design. Replaced by the TestPR416R2_Grandfathering_* regression guards.

findings.title: Grandfathering was removed outright: an existing legacy RBG is frozen -- it cannot even be scaled while compatibility is disabled
findings.detail: PR#414 had ValidateWorkloadTypesUpdate, which grandfathered role names already using a legacy type (PR#414's F10 criticised that rule as too loose). PR#416 dropped the concept: ValidateUpdate now runs validateNoLegacyWorkloads over the whole new object on every UPDATE. So a pre-existing legacy RBG cannot be scaled, cannot have its image changed, and cannot be modified by any client that PUTs the whole object.
findings.observed: Scaling an existing Deployment-typed RBG from 1 to 3 replicas is rejected: 'spec.roles[0] (role "worker"): workload type "apps/v1/Deployment" is not supported when v1alpha1 compatibility is disabled'.
findings.control: control_migration_to_roleinstanceset_allowed PASSES -- switching the role's annotation to RoleInstanceSet is accepted, so one escape hatch does exist and users are not completely stuck. Without this control the finding would have been overstated.
findings.suggestion: Decide explicitly whether existing legacy objects are meant to be frozen or merely prevented from growing. If freezing is intended, say so in the README and surface it as a condition on the object (see F2a) rather than only as an admission error on every write. Allowing replica changes while forbidding new legacy roles is the usual middle ground.
findings.round2Note: Scaling a pre-existing deprecated role is accepted; migrating away is still allowed. Pinned by TestPR416R2_Grandfathering_ExistingRoleStaysWritable.

round3.note: kubectl scale of a pre-existing deprecated role denied again

findings.title: The reconcile path has no compatibility gate: legacy reconcilers are still built, the LWS watch re-arms itself, and both then hit RBAC this PR removed
findings.detail: PR#416 gates exactly three places -- cacheOptions(), the Owns() calls in SetupWithManager, and deleteOrphanRoles. The reconcile path is not gated: getOrCreateWorkloadReconciler (rolebasedgroup_controller.go:590) calls reconciler.NewWorkloadReconciler (pkg/reconciler/workload_reconciler.go:54-69), which takes no flag and returns a Deployment/StatefulSet/LWS reconciler unconditionally. That reconciler reads and writes those types through the cache-backed client, where (a) cacheOptions(true) removed the group-name label selector, so the informer that starts is UNBOUNDED cluster-wide rather than absent -- ByObject is per-type configuration, not an allowlist -- and (b) this same PR removed list/watch/get on those types from the ClusterRole, so that informer can never sync. Separately, the same call site (:614) invokes dynamicWatchCustomCRD, which re-registers Owns(&lwsv1.LeaderWorkerSet{}) at :1619 with NO compatibility check, so the PR description's claim that the controller 'stops watching Deploy/STS/LWS' does not hold for LeaderWorkerSet.
findings.observed: With disableV1alpha1Compatibility=true the controller still built *reconciler.DeploymentReconciler, *reconciler.StatefulSetReconciler and *reconciler.LeaderWorkerSetReconciler for the corresponding workload types.
findings.control: control_roleinstanceset_still_built PASSES, so the factory is functional and the finding is not 'the factory is broken'.
findings.biteCheck: 90-bite-check.sh makes the Deployment case return an error, re-runs the subtest, and it reports 'F3 FIXED'; the edit is reverted and the production diff verified empty.
findings.suggestion: Gate the reconcile path too -- either pass the flag into NewWorkloadReconciler so it refuses legacy types with a clear error, or (better) restore the Step-0 guard from F2a so Reconcile never reaches the factory for a legacy role. Also gate dynamicWatchCustomCRD's LWS branch. And keep the label selector in cacheOptions in BOTH modes: it costs nothing and removing it makes the failure mode strictly worse.
findings.round2Note: The delta only renamed the field. getOrCreateWorkloadReconciler still builds legacy reconcilers with no gate and still calls dynamicWatchCustomCRD, which re-arms the LeaderWorkerSet watch at rolebasedgroup_controller.go:1617-1621 regardless of the flag.
findings.round2Escalation: Code unchanged, CONSEQUENCE escalated. In round 1 the webhook denied the controller's first write, so Reconcile stopped at step 0 and never reached the ungated factory. Round 2 deliberately admits that write (the F2a/F2c/F9/F10 fix), so the ungated path is now REACHED for exactly the pre-existing objects the exemption was written to protect, and fails on Forbidden against statefulsets with no condition and no event. This also makes it a documentation defect: deploy/helm/rbgs/README.md:36-38 now asserts an exempt group "stays writable (and scalable) and the controllers can keep reconciling it" -- the admission clause holds, the reconcile clause does not. README.md:33 and the Go flag help also both say "the controller stops watching them", which dynamicWatchCustomCRD (rolebasedgroup_controller.go:1609) contradicts for LeaderWorkerSet by re-arming the watch at runtime.

round3.note: legacy reconcilers still built when the deprecated types are off

findings.title: The upgrade guard hard-fails the exact command the repo documents for installing, including its own README, the Makefile, the stress script and two CI workflows
findings.detail: templates/upgrade-guard.yaml calls `fail` whenever .Release.IsUpgrade is true. `helm upgrade --install` sets that on the second and every later invocation against the same release -- and that is the command the repo prescribes in 10 places. The sharpest instance is inside the chart's own README: line 33 says "This chart version only supports fresh installation (`helm install`)" and line 123 repeats the warning, yet the Installing section at line 40 tells the user to run `helm upgrade --install`. The guard also breaks `helm rollback` and any GitOps controller (ArgoCD/Flux), which use upgrade semantics.
findings.observed: `helm template --is-upgrade` fails with 'Error: execution error at (rbgs/templates/upgrade-guard.yaml:2:4): Upgrade is not supported for this chart version.' while the plain install render succeeds. 10 call sites invoke helm/`$(HELM)` upgrade: Makefile:253, deploy/helm/rbgs/README.md:40, test/stress/scripts/deploy-controller.sh:52, README.md:77, README-zh_CN.md:77, doc/install.md:30 and :66, doc/dev/how_to_develop.md:294, .github/workflows/e2e-test.yml:158, .github/workflows/release-test.yml:117.
findings.whyCIIsGreen: Every workflow runs `kind create cluster` first (e2e-test.yml:112 and :297, release-test.yml:84 and :215), so the release never pre-exists and IsUpgrade is never true. No CI job installs the chart twice, which makes this entire class invisible to CI -- the same blind spot that let PR#414's render blocker through.
findings.liveNote: The end-to-end arm (real `helm install` then real `helm upgrade`) was NOT run. This chart's ClusterRole/ClusterRoleBinding/ValidatingWebhookConfiguration have fixed names and would overwrite the unrelated rbgs controller already live in rbg-system on the shared review cluster. `helm template --is-upgrade` is a complete and deterministic proof of the guard's behaviour, and the call-site list is a static fact, so the mutating arm adds confirmation rather than evidence. Run it on a throwaway cluster if wanted.
findings.suggestion: If upgrades must be blocked, at minimum update the 10 documented call sites in the same PR (they currently contradict the guard), and prefer a targeted check -- e.g. fail only when upgrading ACROSS the incompatible version boundary, by comparing the previous release's chart version -- over an unconditional `fail` that also blocks value-only changes, rollbacks and same-version redeploys.
findings.round2Note: The upgrade guard still hard-fails 'helm upgrade --install', which the repo documents in 10 call sites including the chart's own README, which both forbids and prescribes it.

round3.note: upgrade guard still hard-fails 'helm upgrade --install'; its remediation text is the R3-F22 bypass

findings.title: The new compatibility block is the one block in the chart that dereferences values unguarded, so a partially-written block either hard-fails the render or SILENTLY strips the controller's RBAC
findings.detail: Four templates dereference .Values.compatibility.v1alpha1.enabled directly (clusterrole.yaml:76 and :119, manager.yaml:51, NOTES.txt:19). Every pre-existing block uses the defensive `| default dict` idiom (manager.yaml:31, :41, :42, :49). Consequence: a `compatibility:` key that is present but incomplete does NOT coalesce to the chart default. NOTE FOR THE AUTHOR: this is the concern Copilot raised on PR#413 and PR#414 and was wrong about both times -- it was correctly disproved there because those blocks were guarded. It is real here, for the new block only.
findings.observed: `compatibility:` with no children and `compatibility.v1alpha1:` with no children both HARD-FAIL: 'nil pointer evaluating interface {}.v1alpha1' / '.enabled' at clusterrole.yaml:76. `compatibility: {}` fails with "can't evaluate field v1alpha1 in type interface {}". Worse, `compatibility.v1alpha1.enabled:` left blank renders fine but evaluates falsy, SILENTLY stripping all 8 legacy RBAC rules without the operator asking.
findings.control: --set controller.features=null and --set global=null both render 12/12 valid documents, so the defect is specific to the new unguarded block and not a general property of the chart or of helm value coalescing.
findings.suggestion: Use the same idiom as the rest of the chart, e.g. `{{- $compat := (.Values.compatibility | default dict).v1alpha1 | default dict }}{{- if $compat.enabled }}`, and define the intended default in exactly one place. This also removes the silent-strip shape.
findings.round2Note: The dangerous direction is now unreachable: no value shape yields flag-enabled + RBAC-stripped (disproved across 13 shapes). But the value is consumed by two different predicates, which opens R2-F11 and R2-F12.

findings.title: Regression guard: PR#414's render blocker does not recur -- all documents are valid offline and accepted by a real API server

findings.observed: 12/12 documents valid on each of the three valid value shapes, and a live k8s v1.36.1 API server accepts all 12 under both the default and compat-disabled shapes. The apiVersion-less control object is correctly rejected by the same command, so the check is not vacuously green.
findings.round2Note: A real API server accepts all 12 rendered documents in both toggle states. Note the round-1 script tested the default twice because its second shape used the removed value path; retargeted, so this is now non-vacuous.

round3.note: a real API server accepts all 12 rendered objects in both shapes

findings.title: Disabling compatibility does not restrict v1alpha1-era workload types -- it makes the ENTIRE v1alpha1 API unusable, including for users who never chose a workload type
findings.detail: Three links compose: (1) v1alpha1 RoleSpec.Workload has a CRD default of {apps/v1, StatefulSet} (rolebasedgroup_types.go:341) applied by the API SERVER, so the field is never empty -- proven read-only against live k8s v1.36.1; (2) convertRoleV1alpha1ToV2 unconditionally copies it into the role-workload-type annotation (conversion.go:142-148), behind a guard that the default renders permanently true; (3) validateNoLegacyWorkloads rejects exactly that value. The PR bills itself as an interim RBAC reduction whose migration path is deferred to a follow-up, but as written it removes the API that follow-up is meant to migrate.
findings.controls: Same converted object accepted with compat enabled; a v1alpha1 role survives only if the user explicitly writes the v1alpha2 RoleInstanceSet type into the v1alpha1 workload field -- which bounds the finding while showing that path is unusable as a migration story.
findings.seeAlso: F8b extends this to RoleBasedGroupSet, so a fix confined to the RBG validator is insufficient.
findings.round2Note: Acknowledged rather than fixed: the v1alpha1 schema still defaults spec.roles[].workload to apps/v1 StatefulSet, so a v1alpha1 object is rejected on CREATE unless every role names RoleInstanceSet explicitly. The delta documents the trap in the flag help and the chart README instead of removing it.

round3.note: v1alpha1 defaulting still makes the whole v1alpha1 API unusable when disabled (now documented)

findings.title: The F8 defaulting chain also reaches RoleBasedGroupSet, so every v1alpha1 RBGSet is rejected wholesale too
findings.detail: The v1alpha1 rolebasedgroupsets schema carries the same StatefulSet default on spec.template.roles[].workload (config/crd/bases/...rolebasedgroupsets.yaml:16672-16681) and rolebasedgroupset_conversion.go:37 routes through the same convertRoleV1alpha1ToV2. findings.round2Note: The same defaulting chain still rejects every v1alpha1 RoleBasedGroupSet wholesale on create.

round3.note: same for RoleBasedGroupSet

findings.title: RBGSet child-sync is denied by the new UPDATE rule: a pre-existing RBGSet with a legacy template error-loops forever (PR#414 F7 recurring)
findings.detail: rolebasedgroupset_controller.go:465 copies groupTemplate.spec.roles onto the child RBG and calls client.Update. That is an UPDATE on rolebasedgroups, so the new rule denies it for a legacy-typed template. The new RoleBasedGroupSetValidator only guards NEW RBGSets; objects already in the cluster are never re-validated, and the child-sync path is exactly where PR#414 F7 returns. The sync is idempotent (identical roles) and still rejected.
findings.round2Note: The update leg is fixed (rolebasedgroupset_controller.go:465 template sync is accepted). The CREATE leg is not: see R2-F13.

findings.title: HPA-driven autoscaling of a legacy RBG fails: the scale path writes the RBG main resource and is denied
findings.detail: rolebasedgroupscalingadapter_controller.go:511 (updateRoleReplicas) sets role.Replicas and calls client.Update on the RBG. This is the scale-subresource/HPA path (ScaleTargetRef, pkg/scale). retry.RetryOnConflict only retries Conflict, so an admission Forbidden propagates straight out. This reframes F2c: the real consequence is not that users cannot scale, but that HPA cannot.
findings.round2Note: The ScalingAdapter replica update at rolebasedgroupscalingadapter_controller.go:511 is accepted. Proved against the real updateRoleReplicas with the adapter object present, so ValidateScalingAdapterReplicas actually runs.

findings.title: Migrating an LWS-backed role to RoleInstanceSet silently renames the pod env contract, breaking user containers at runtime
findings.detail: LWS injected LWS_LEADER_ADDRESS / LWS_GROUP_SIZE / LWS_WORKER_INDEX; the RoleInstanceSet path injects RBG_LWP_LEADER_ADDRESS / RBG_LWP_GROUP_SIZE / RBG_LWP_WORKER_INDEX. Same semantics, different names, no aliases. The RBG is admitted, the pods run, and the failure happens inside the user process -- no admission error, no reconcile error, nothing on the RBG status. RBG already declares DeprecatedEnvLws* constants for a shim but references them nowhere. Secondary: LwsWorkerIndexLabelKey is also a dead constant, so the leaderworkerset.sigs.k8s.io/worker-index label disappears too.
findings.harnessBites: The test fails outright if the replacement RBG_LWP_* variables are absent, so it cannot pass or fail vacuously.
findings.note: This is NOT a defect of PR#416 itself -- it is a consequence of the planned LWS removal that PR#416 is the first step toward. Raise it against the removal timeline, not this PR.

round3.note: LWS_* -> RBG_LWP_* env rename still has no alias shim; untouched by the delta

findings.title: NOTE: deleteOrphanRoles still skips legacy cleanup when compatibility is disabled (PR#414's F6, unchanged)
findings.detail: rolebasedgroup_controller.go:679-694 wraps the Deployment/StatefulSet/LWS CleanupOrphanedWorkloads calls in `if !r.disableV1alpha1Compatibility`. Cleaning up already-created legacy workloads is a different concern from managing new ones; if the skip stays, the delete RBAC must be retained or cleanup will 403 when compatibility is re-enabled. Carried from PR#413/#414. NOT re-tested live: on a real cluster an owner-referenced orphan disappears within ~10s in BOTH modes and also with no controller running at all, because Kubernetes GC is the actor, so a live test cannot discriminate. Do NOT claim 'leaks indefinitely' -- only the code-level skip is established.
findings.round2Note: deleteOrphanRoles still skips legacy cleanup when the types are disabled; rename only.

findings.claim: The RoleBasedGroupSet's own UPDATE is grandfathered, but the child RoleBasedGroup its controller must CREATE (rolebasedgroupset_controller.go:231) is not, because ValidateCreate still runs the strict whole-object check. A pre-existing RBGSet whose template uses a deprecated workload type can no longer scale up or replace a deleted child; the controller retries the denied create forever.
aggravating: spec.replicas on RoleBasedGroupSet is a scale subresource (rolebasedgroupset_types.go:77) and the webhook rule does not cover rolebasedgroupsets/scale, so an HPA can raise replicas without admission ever seeing it; the refusal then happens asynchronously inside the controller.
scaleUp's error short-circuits Reconcile at :184-189, BEFORE updateStatus at :332, so the object does not even record the failure -- round 1's 'no sign on the object' complaint recurs verbatim.
Reachable with zero user action: a child lost to GC or an accidental delete can never be replaced.

findings.claim: A string-typed false renders flag=false but leaves the deprecated RBAC in place. manager.yaml:57 PRINTS the value while clusterrole.yaml:12 tests Go-template truthiness, and a non-empty string is truthy. The operator stops using the deprecated types while keeping full create/delete/patch on them -- the exact permissions this PR exists to remove -- and nothing warns. Reachable via --set-string, a quoted enabled: "false", or ArgoCD forceString. Same for "0", "f", "F", "False", "FALSE".

findings.claim: The generator's deprecated-resource list is a third hand-maintained copy of 'which workload types are deprecated' (alongside isDeprecatedWorkloadType in rolebasedgroup_validation.go and the gated Owns() calls in rolebasedgroup_controller.go). A resource missing from it is emitted OUTSIDE the conditional, i.e. granted even when the toggle is off -- it fails OPEN (over-grant), with no test and no CI signal. findings.claim: The chart README value-table row says the webhook 'rejects roles that use' a deprecated type, contradicting the prose three lines below it, NOTES.txt, values.yaml and the Go flag help, all of which correctly say roles that ALREADY use one are exempt. The table row is the only place with the stricter wording, and it describes the behaviour this delta specifically removed.

round3.note: chart README value-table row no longer contradicts the prose below it

findings.claim: `rbg rollout undo` (cmd/cli/cmd/rollout/rollout_undo.go:123) restores roles from a ControllerRevision, so rolling back across a workload-type change or a role rename is refused while the toggle is off -- a documented user-facing feature failing with an update-path message about a 'newly added role'.

The exemption is keyed by role NAME, so renaming a role that already carries a deprecated type reads as 'newly added' and is denied: roles in a pre-existing deprecated object can never be renamed while the toggle is off. NOT reachable as a controller operation -- an RBGSet template rename is refused at the parent, so it never propagates to a child. Reorder IS handled correctly. Accepted as reasonable; the 'newly added role' wording is the confusing part.

NEGATIVE RESULT (checked, no defect): the delta check cannot misfire via conversion. Both CRDs have storageversion v1alpha2 and the webhook is registered for v1alpha2, so oldObject is read from etcd already in the webhook's version and is never conversion-derived; GetWorkloadType() returns the same string on both sides across a v1alpha1 round-trip. No reachable path makes oldRoles empty. This is now a constraint the design DEPENDS on: if oldObject ever became conversion-derived, every role would look newly added.

NEGATIVE RESULT (checked, no defect): status subresource writes bypass the webhook (the rule lists rolebasedgroups / rolebasedgroupsets, not .../status), so no status write is denied. Related near-miss worth one sentence in review: syncRBGMetadata (rolebasedgroupset_controller.go:497-506) wipes the child's metadata.annotations, which would be a second blocker if the workload-type annotation lived there -- it lives on RoleSpec.Annotations, so it is safe, but only by one field location.

The PR description still describes the round-1 design, so two of the three documents round 1's F1 named were corrected and the third was not. At this head the body still says `compatibility.v1alpha1.enabled` (renamed), "(default: `false`)" (now true), `--disable-v1alpha1-compatibility` (renamed AND inverted), and "the validating webhook rejects RBGs/RBGSets using legacy workload types" -- which is no longer true for UPDATE, the single most important behavioural change in this delta. Nothing ships from the PR description, but it is what reviewers read and it tends to become the squash message and the changelog entry. Related to R2-F19, which is the same class of defect inside the chart README.

findings.title: The 'fresh installation only' premise the whole design rests on is enforced nowhere, and the repo documents the bypass in four places
findings.detail: PR #416 justifies having no grandfathering, no conversion and no migration with one claim: 'the sole supported way to reach false is a fresh install, where no such object can exist', enforced by templates/upgrade-guard.yaml. Four structural facts show that guard does not cover the case that matters. (1) The chart declares no CRDs -- crds/ is empty and no template emits a CustomResourceDefinition (they come from the crd-upgrade pre-install Job) -- so helm uninstall removes neither the CRDs nor any RoleBasedGroup/RoleBasedGroupSet; those objects survive. (2) The guard keys on .Release.IsUpgrade, false on a reinstall (control: helm template --is-upgrade does fail, a plain render does not). (3) The repo instructs exactly that path in four places: upgrade-guard.yaml:2 'Please uninstall and reinstall', NOTES.txt:17, chart README.md:65 and README.md:155. (4) Nothing inspects the cluster -- no template uses Helm lookup, and the enabled=false render succeeds unconditionally. So the documented update procedure yields a fresh release over surviving objects with the toggle settable to false in the same command, producing exactly the state the PR says cannot exist. Consequences are already proved RED at this head by the round-1 write-path tests: the discovery annotation patch, kubectl scale, the RBGSet template sync, the HPA scale path and the child RBG create are all denied, with nothing written to the object's status.
findings.proposedFix: A pre-install check that fails the install when enabled=false and any RoleBasedGroup/RoleBasedGroupSet already uses a deprecated workload type. The crd-upgrade Job is the in-chart precedent (its own ServiceAccount, pre-install hook). This makes the premise real and closes F2a/F2c/F9/F10/R2-F13 as a class, rather than one path per round.

findings.title: The dropped-rule guard added for R2-F15 is a count comparison that a rule split masks, so it cannot fire -- slack is already 2 at this head
findings.detail: 68850e6f answers R2-F15 with 'if len(blocks) < len(role.Rules) { return error }' in run(). But splitRules is not count-preserving: a rule whose resources straddle the gate emits two blocks (one kept, one gated), so a split inflates the count and pays for a drop. Measured against the committed config/rbac/role.yaml: 16 rules -> 18 blocks, because the apps rule (controllerrevisions+deployments+statefulsets) and its /status counterpart both straddle. The guard therefore tolerates two silently dropped rules today: adding one urls= kubebuilder marker strips that permission from the chart ClusterRole with exit 0, no error and no CI diff. The PR's own TestSplitRulesDropsResourcelessRule asserts assert.Empty(t, blocks) with no error, pinning the drop as acceptable at the splitRules level -- so the fix is tested at the wrong layer.
findings.proposedFix: Reject any input rule that produced no output block (per-rule coverage) instead of comparing totals. Harness-bites check confirmed: adding that check turns all three R3 generator tests green, and requires updating TestSplitRulesDropsResourcelessRule.

liveNote: L3 is READ-ONLY on the shared ACK cluster: 20-live-dryrun.sh prefixes every object with pr416dry-, retargets namespaced objects to `default`, and uses only --dry-run=server. Round 2 fixed its second shape, which still used the removed compatibility.v1alpha1.enabled path and was therefore re-rendering the default: it now uses controller.deprecatedWorkloadTypes.enabled=false. 12/12 objects accepted in both shapes. The mutating arms were deliberately not run because this chart's cluster-scoped object names are fixed and would overwrite the unrelated rbgs controller live in rbg-system. To run them, use a throwaway cluster: (1) helm install, then helm upgrade --install again, and expect the second to fail at upgrade-guard.yaml (F4); (2) install with the deprecated types enabled, create an RBGSet whose template uses StatefulSet, flip the toggle off, then raise replicas and watch the child create be denied with nothing written to the RBGSet status (R2-F13).

designNotes.conclusion: Gate on cluster state (deprecated-workload objects; v1alpha1-era objects), not on chart version numbers, carried by a pre-install,pre-upgrade hook Job with hook-weight below crd-upgrade's -4. One mechanism closes F4 and R3-F22, and the documented 'helm upgrade --install' becomes idempotent again so none of the 10 call sites need changing.
measuredFacts: The previous chart version is NOT readable from a template: the Deployment carries no version label, and the release Secret's `version` label is the revision number ('1') while the chart version is gzipped inside data.

lookup is EMPTY on helm template, --is-upgrade and client-side --dry-run; populated only on a real install/upgrade or --dry-run=server. A fail-closed TEMPLATE check therefore false-fails helm diff upgrade.
semverCompare '< 0.8.0-alpha.3' is correct on all 8 prerelease/release cases, so version comparison is not the risky part of the design.

CRD status.storedVersions is readable via lookup (this cluster: [v1alpha2]) and is maintained by Kubernetes, but it is STICKY -- it only shrinks when an operator patches it, so it must corroborate rather than gate.

A failing pre-upgrade hook Job leaves the release 'failed' with a recorded revision, but a subsequent normal upgrade succeeds WITHOUT --force. A template-level fail aborts at render time and leaves the release untouched.
helm diff upgrade does not execute hooks at all, so a hook-based check cannot false-fail it -- the decisive advantage over a template check.
designNotes.rejectedOption: A chart-version marker ConfigMap + semverCompare was built and tested end-to-end (all 6 scenarios behave correctly), but it CANNOT deliver the stated intent: the marker ships with this PR while 0.8.0-alpha.3 is already released without it, so an upgrade from alpha.3 always lands in the 'cannot tell' branch. Related trap: the PR branch's Chart.yaml is still 0.8.0-alpha.2, below the threshold, so shipping as-is would have the chart's own guard refuse the next upgrade.
designNotes.safety: Read-only against the shared cluster except two throwaway namespaces (pr416-guard-test, pr416-hook-test) holding a scratch chart whose only real resource is a ConfigMap. No cluster-scoped object created, so no collision with the unrelated rbgs release in rbg-system. Both namespaces removed by an EXIT trap.
